stories.title: Bank of America hit with $1.2bn fine for money laundering failings
stories.summary: Bank of America has been fined $1.2bn (£910m) for failing to detect potential money laundering and other illegal activity, the US Treasury Department said on Tuesday. The announcement came less 24 hours before Bank of America was due to announce its quarterly earnings on Wednesday morning.
stories.why: Large regulatory penalties can expose compliance failures and raise costs or scrutiny for major financial institutions.

stories.title: India and US move closer to trade deal, says External Affairs Minister
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said that India and the United States are moving closer to finalising a bilateral trade agreement. He noted that both sides are working on remaining issues, but the talks are complicated by the United States striking competitive agreements with other economies. Jaishankar also highlighted the role of tariffs as the US seeks to reindustrialise its economy, underscoring their relevance to the negotiations.
stories.why: The negotiations matter because they aim to resolve outstanding trade issues and tariff arrangements between the two countries.

stories.title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
stories.summary: Only five years into its journey, Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and have conversations with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a slew of lawsuits and struggles to scale its popular platform. In a court document, the company said it had assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.

stories.title: IMF raises 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% while warning of AI and debt risks
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund modestly upgraded its outlook for 2026, projecting world GDP growth of 3.1%, up from the July estimate of 3.0% but still below the 3.5% expected for 2025. In its Economic Outlook released in Bangkok during the IMF‑World Bank fall meetings, the IMF cautioned that a rapid AI‑driven market correction, potential job losses, and rising sovereign debt pose heightened risks to the recovery.
stories.why: The warning signals that emerging AI‑related financial turbulence and debt vulnerabilities could undermine the modest growth gains.

stories.title: RBI open to more steps to curb FX speculation, Governor Sanjay Malhotra says
stories.summary: RBI open to more steps to curb FX speculation, Governor Sanjay Malhotra says RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the central bank may take further steps to curb speculative forex trading and ensure orderly movement in the currency market. He said recent restrictions aim to support genuine hedging needs, not impose capital controls.
stories.why: This matters because it could affect India’s economy, major industries, investment, jobs or trade.

stories.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
stories.summary: Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. While PRIMA is commercially available in Europe for patients who’ve lost their sight to geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases, including Stargardt disease, which is currently considered incurable.
